title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LLTO material. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. The LLZO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability and sinterability at a lower cost.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability of the cell.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression during fast charging.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Ag-C layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The LATP and LLTO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the cycle life is improved.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The LATP and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability in contact with lithium.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide glass ceramic solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 crystal phase with controlled crystallinity and widened electrochemical window
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte is a glass ceramic in which a Li7P3S11 crystal phase is precipitated in a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 70:30 and containing LiI in an amount of 3 mol% to 8 mol%. A glass obtained by mechanical amorphization of the raw materials in a planetary mill is heat-treated at 260 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 1 hour to 3 hours, just above the crystallization onset, so that the metastable Li7P3S11 phase precipitates with a crystallite size of 30 nm to 150 nm while devitrification to the low-conductivity Li4P2S6 phase is kept to 3% or less. The degree of crystallinity is 60% to 85%, the residual glassy phase deforms plastically during cold pressing, and the glass ceramic has an ionic conductivity of 4.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C with an activation energy of 0.22 eV. The iodide widens the electrochemical window on the reduction side to 1.6 V versus Li/Li+. The glass ceramic is distinguished from crystalline Li6PS5Cl or Li3PS4 powders by the presence of the vitreous phase and gives an all-solid-state battery with improved cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7% after 100 cycles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The resulting LLTO and LATP material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The LLTO and LATP material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with aluminum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1150 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. The LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.
