A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a zinc additive. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering for lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A sheet of 30 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tantalum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The roll temperature is 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window and cycle life of the solid-state battery.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The content of Li2O is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

assignee_std: DRIOSTUS ADVANCED MATERIALS TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation for lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The mixed halogen substitution improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and tin substitution for improved moisture stability
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid is a crystallized glass comprising a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 75:25 in which 2 mol% to 6 mol% of the phosphorus is substituted by tin, and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated from the matrix. A glassy precursor prepared by melt quenching at 750 degrees C is reheated at 240 degrees C to 280 degrees C so that the beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 100 nm and a degree of crystallinity of 50% to 75%. The tin, a soft acid, binds the sulfur more strongly than phosphorus, and the cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 60 minutes is 8 cm3/g or less. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and retains 80% or more of the conductivity after the exposure. Unlike crystalline Li7P3S11 or Li6PS5Cl powders, the remaining vitreous phase gives good deformability, and an all-solid-state battery using the material shows improved cycle life.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved high-voltage stability and rate performance.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Specific examples are Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The oxygen content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Solvent-free self-supporting sulfide ion-conductive solid sheet bound by a fibrillated fluoropolymer network and method of forming the same
abstract: A self-supporting sheet comprises particles of an argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid of the Li6PS5Cl type and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 3 wt%, the binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without any solvent. The sheet is formed by kneading the powder and the binder under a shear rate of 200 s^-1 to 800 s^-1 at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C so that the binder is fibrillized, rolling the kneaded mass between a pair of rollers heated to 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and calendering the rolled film in at least three passes with a stepwise reduced roller gap to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 300 nm, and the sheet has a porosity of 8% or less, a tensile strength of 1.5 MPa or more, and an ionic conductivity of 2.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Because no polar solvent contacts the sulfide, the conductivity of the powder is retained, and the sheet can be wound on a roll and laminated onto an electrode without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability in production and improved cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tantalum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided.
