A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, LLZO, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4, LLZO, and LATP material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability and simpler handling.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The tin content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which silver is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A precursor of the LATP and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved grain boundary resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with gallium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The LLTO and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. A precursor of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved cycle life compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The bilayer structure improves the moisture stability compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The low electronic conductivity of the Li2ZrO3 and LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO, Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved dendrite suppression and operates at a lower stack pressure.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LATP material. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
