The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An argyrodite ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LGPS material. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which titanium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4, LLZO, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Ag-C layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance.

title: Germanium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 1.5 mA/cm2. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The LLZO and LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tungsten and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using 1,2-dimethoxyethane for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved sinterability and rate capability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and moisture stability.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. Specific examples are Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved electrochemical window and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A precursor of the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The tin substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability of the cell.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The LiF, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better interfacial resistance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li3PS4 material. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. With tin substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide.
