In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by atomic layer deposition. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, LiF, and LLZO material. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability and sinterability.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity of the layer.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The Li3PS4 and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the electrochemical window.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved sinterability and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The content of P2O5 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The content of Li2O is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by thermal evaporation followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ion-conductive solid in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ScBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The resulting LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The LLZO, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture.
