The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and production method thereof
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A precursor of the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method prevents short circuit and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C in an oven. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and sinterability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. In the trigonal structure, indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxidation potential is 4.5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved electrochemical window.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability of the cell.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The LATP and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The LATP and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with LiF is described. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The LLZO and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material.
