abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved electrochemical window and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, LiF, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with a gradient lithium niobate coating layer whose outer region contains lithium indium chloride
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide with a nickel content of 85 mol% or more and a gradient coating layer having an average thickness of 8 nm to 25 nm. The inner region of the coating layer adjacent to the core consists of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the outer region contains lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) dispersed in the niobate so that the indium content increases continuously from 0 at% at the core to 15 at% to 30 at% at the outer surface. The coating layer is formed by applying a niobium alkoxide solution, heat-treating at 320 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and then applying an alcoholic solution of Li3InCl6 followed by vacuum drying. The niobate inner region blocks the formation of a space-charge layer and the diffusion of nickel into the sulfide, while the chloride-rich outer region, stable up to 4.3 V versus Li/Li+ and conductive to lithium ions, lowers the charge transfer resistance with Li6PS5Cl. The coverage is 92% or more and the interfacial resistance after 100 cycles at 4.3 V is 15 ohm cm2 or less. When the sulfide is a glass ceramic, the coated material further improves the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The oxygen substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The Li3PS4 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7% after 100 cycles. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ErBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The LLTO and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the cycle life of the product.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved high-voltage stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.045 or less. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. An ionic conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The LLZO, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with niobium and sintered with Al2O3 is described. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LGPS material. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
