abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Zirconium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and production method thereof
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity of the layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and production method thereof
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The LATP and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The resulting LiNbO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with gallium and sintered with LiF is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A precursor of the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). With germanium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6. The LLZO and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3InCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. A precursor of the LLTO and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The LLTO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the cycle life.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl.
