The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The Li3N layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The arsenic-free antimony content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A precursor of the LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.2 to 0.45, and a method for producing the same are provided. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3% after 100 cycles. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiF and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and the critical current density is 1.5 mA/cm2. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The viscosity of 2000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tantalum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP, LLTO, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The tin substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 30% or less is provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 15%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The content of LiI is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The LATP and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The tin content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided.
