The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the interfacial resistance.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with an indium additive. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium bromide framework. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. A precursor of the LLZO and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The content of P2O5 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The LiF and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Niobium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of erbium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the solid-state cell.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. The content of P2O5 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The tin content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 30% or less is provided. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The LiF and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Bromine-containing argyrodite solid electrolyte with suppressed lithium chloride impurity and improved moisture stability
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein a = x + y, 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5. Replacing part of the chlorine with bromine expands the lattice and raises the anion disorder on the 4a and 4d sites, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway, while the halogen-rich composition is fired at 460 degrees C to 520 degrees C so that a lithium chloride impurity phase does not precipitate. In an X-ray diffraction pattern measured with CuK-alpha radiation, the ratio of the peak intensity at 2-theta = 34.8 degrees attributed to LiCl to the peak intensity at 30.0 degrees attributed to the argyrodite phase is 0.05 or less. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 7 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C, retains 85% or more of the conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, and keeps the argyrodite phase without a glass ceramic by-product. Compared with Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 type conductors, the material gives an all-solid-state battery with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.045 or less. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step.
