The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Germanium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. With germanium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a solid electrolyte layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LATP and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The LLTO and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte stable above 4.8 V
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tantalum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The content of P2O5 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material. A precursor of the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the cycle life.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tantalum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Hafnium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and cycle life.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ScBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In the trigonal structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more.
