The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The resulting LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3YCl6. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the interfacial resistance and dendrite suppression.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. A solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The LATP material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Slurry composition for casting a garnet ceramic ion conductor layer with a nonpolar solvent and a rubber binder
abstract: A slurry composition for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) particles having a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder in an amount of 2 wt% to 6 wt% relative to the particles, an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, the slurry having a solid content of 55 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 800 mPa s to 2500 mPa s at 25 degrees C. The slurry is cast by a doctor blade onto a release film at 2 m/min to 8 m/min, dried at 70 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the dried layer of 15 micrometers to 40 micrometers is peeled from the release film and transferred onto an electrode by pressing. A lithium borate glass ceramic in an amount of 3 wt% to 10 wt% is mixed into the slurry so that, after a short heat treatment at 400 degrees C, the glass ceramic bonds the garnet particles and lowers the interfacial resistance between particles. The layer retains 80% or more of the conductivity of the pressed powder, and the slurry shows improved sheet formability on a roll-to-roll coater.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The substitution amount is 10 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. With germanium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF, Li3YCl6, and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A precursor of the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A precursor of the LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved cycle life.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and method for producing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
