abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with aluminum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP, LLTO, and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved sheet formability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved cycle life and simpler handling.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance and dendrite suppression.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the dendrite suppression.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state lithium battery. The method shortens the process and improves the electrochemical window of the layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A precursor of the LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with gallium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state lithium battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and moisture stability of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A precursor of the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the cycle life.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and sheet formability of the layer.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life during fast charging.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The solid electrolyte provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.
