The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a zinc additive. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The low electronic conductivity of the LiF and Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

assignee_std: CORAST INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state battery including the sheet are described. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved moisture stability and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The widened electrochemical window improves the electrochemical window of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved electrochemical window.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The content of GeS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The resulting Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The resulting Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The content of Li2O is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A precursor of the Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3InCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved cycle life and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using acetonitrile for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The low electronic conductivity of the LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3).
