The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with an indium additive. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Specific examples are Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 16% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The LiF and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The LLZO, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state lithium battery. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tantalum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Ag-C layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved moisture stability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by thermal evaporation followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Li3N layer of 50 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A precursor of the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. The Li3InCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The LATP and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The Li3N layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity during fast charging.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and method for producing the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with niobium and sintered with LiF is described. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with gallium and sintered with LiF is described. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The resulting LiF and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The Li3YCl6, LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO material. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and LLTO material. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a magnesium additive. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the high-voltage stability of the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder.
