The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The resulting LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the layer.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The LGPS and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved electrochemical window.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life of the layer.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The content of P2O5 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life and sheet formability of the cell.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The content of LiI is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the electrochemical window.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V for lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. The additive content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Al2O3 inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The resulting LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
