abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A precursor of the LLZO, LATP, and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. With hafnium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LGPS material. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The LLTO and LATP material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1230 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.3 to 0.75. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In the trigonal structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a magnesium additive. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved electrochemical window and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the solid-state cell.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in anisole with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the interfacial resistance and dendrite suppression.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The resulting LATP, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and LLZO material. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The method prevents short circuit and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance.
