The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Zirconium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability in contact with lithium.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The tin content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The method prevents short circuit and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and method for producing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming an ion-conductive solid sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 1.5 mA/cm2. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The arsenic-free antimony content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sheet formability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a lithium fluoride-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The resulting Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the dendrite suppression of the cell.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.2 to 0.45, and a method for producing the same are provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved sinterability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with an indium additive. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The LLTO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life during fast charging.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The LATP and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals.
