The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tantalum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The resulting LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Niobium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability and simpler handling.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a magnesium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The resulting Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The LLTO, LLZO, and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved cycle life and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The LiF, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ion-conductive solid in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In the monoclinic structure, indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life.

title: Zirconium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The resulting Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LATP material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The oxygen substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. With hafnium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The resulting LLTO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying.
