A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A precursor of the LLZO and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The resulting Li3YCl6 and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The material comprises Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. With tin substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved interfacial resistance and rate performance.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3YCl6. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. With a binder content of 0.5 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.15 or less. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved moisture stability.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The content of SiS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the solid-state lithium battery.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved sheet formability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Hafnium-substituted NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). With hafnium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A precursor of the LLTO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the lithium metal battery.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6 and LiF material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3InCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The low electronic conductivity of the LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery.
