A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and moisture stability of the solid-state battery.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LATP material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state lithium battery. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by atomic layer deposition. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The resulting Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. The viscosity of 2000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LATP material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and moisture stability at a lower cost.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li2ZrO3, LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. A precursor of the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided.
