A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 15%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression during fast charging.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A precursor of the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance of the layer.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression during fast charging.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The ion-conductive solid shows improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A precursor of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 2 mA/cm2. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the layer.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The Li3PS4 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3PS4, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved moisture stability.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Hafnium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and cycle life and simpler handling.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided.
