The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4, LATP, and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sheet formability.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The resulting Li3YCl6 and LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. In the trigonal structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A precursor of the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The content of Li2O is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The resulting LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C in an oven. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3YCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity during fast charging.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The LiNbO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The resulting Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3YCl6. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3YCl6 material. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the high-voltage stability are improved.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The silicon substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. With germanium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO material. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The bilayer structure improves the dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Tin-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tungsten and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less.
