A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the indium in a lithium indium bromide framework. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In the trigonal structure, indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 15%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1230 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. The method prevents short circuit and improves the ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium indium chloride and to a method for producing the same. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.3 to 0.75. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The method prevents short circuit and improves the ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium bromide ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with aluminum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The bilayer structure improves the dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The LiF and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and LiNbO3 material. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li2ZrO3 and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The substitution amount is 10 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the dendrite suppression is retained.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity of the layer.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. With tin substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of erbium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and lithium battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance and sheet formability of the cell.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the cycle life.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The content of P2O5 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF).
