The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. In the trigonal structure, scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The resulting Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.

title: Tin-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability and sinterability at a lower cost.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, LLZO, and LATP material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The LATP, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In the trigonal structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Tin-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and production method thereof
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The resulting LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The content of P2O5 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved moisture stability and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 30% or less is provided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The roll temperature is 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The method gives reproducible densification and improved cycle life at a lower cost.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The resulting Li3YCl6 and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication.
