A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The LiF layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The LGPS material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved sinterability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the moisture stability of the solid-state cell.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The LiF layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A precursor of the LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The LLZO, LLTO, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A precursor of the LLZO, LLTO, and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state battery. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The content of GeS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. The LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The LiF material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The silicon content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.15 or less. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6.
