The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the cell.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1150 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved sinterability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The Ag-C layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The low electronic conductivity of the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a zinc additive. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Zirconium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 50 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The tensile strength is 1.2 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved electrochemical window.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state lithium battery using it. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the solid-state battery.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A precursor of the LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Germanium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. With germanium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A precursor of the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 10% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life without a thick protective layer.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
