Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The resulting Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. A solid-state battery using the layer shows improved cycle life and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LiNbO3, and Li6PS5Cl material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and interfacial resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and method for producing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The viscosity of 2000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The LiNbO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The low electronic conductivity of the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The method prevents short circuit and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation for lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and method for preparing the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The LiF, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 50 nm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The LiPON layer of 50 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Ag-C layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium indium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a zinc additive. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LiNbO3, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The resulting Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
